title: Genesis Chapter 24 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Genesis chapter 24 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Genesis Chapter 24 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Genesis Chapter 24.

questions.question: Who did Abraham instruct his eldest servant to find a wife for?
options: His son Isaac
His brother Nahor
His nephew Laban
His son Ishmael
questions.correctAnswer: His son Isaac
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:4 says Abraham commanded his servant to take a wife unto his son Isaac.

questions.question: What did Abraham make his servant swear by?
options: The LORD, the God of heaven and earth
The God of Abraham only
The God of the Canaanites
The king of Mesopotamia
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD, the God of heaven and earth
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:3 states Abraham made the servant swear by the LORD, the God of heaven and earth.

questions.question: True or False: Abraham told his servant to take a wife for Isaac from the daughters of the Canaanites.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:3 says Abraham told the servant not to take a wife from the daughters of the Canaanites.

questions.question: What did the servant take with him when he departed to find a wife for Isaac?
options: Ten camels
Five horses
Twenty donkeys
Thirty sheep
questions.correctAnswer: Ten camels
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:10 records that the servant took ten camels of his master.

questions.question: Where did the servant go to find a wife for Isaac?
options: Mesopotamia, city of Nahor
Egypt, city of Goshen
Canaan, city of Hebron
Babylon, city of Babel
questions.correctAnswer: Mesopotamia, city of Nahor
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:10 states the servant went to Mesopotamia, to the city of Nahor.

questions.question: True or False: The servant put his hand under Abraham's thigh to swear the oath.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:9 says the servant put his hand under Abraham's thigh and swore.

questions.question: At what time of day did the servant find the well where women came to draw water?
options: Evening
Morning
Noon
Midnight
questions.correctAnswer: Evening
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:11 says the servant made his camels kneel by the well in the evening, the time women go out to draw water.

questions.question: What sign did the servant pray for to identify the right woman for Isaac?
options: A woman who offers him a drink and also offers to water his camels
A woman who greets him with bread
A woman who does not speak
A woman who comes running to him
questions.correctAnswer: A woman who offers him a drink and also offers to water his camels
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:14 says the servant prayed that the woman who offers him a drink and offers to water his camels would be the one appointed for Isaac.

questions.question: True or False: Rebekah was the daughter of Bethuel, son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:15 and 24:24 identify Rebekah as the daughter of Bethuel, son of Milcah, wife of Nahor.

questions.question: What did Rebekah do when the servant asked for a drink of water?
options: She gave him water and also watered his camels
She refused to give him water
She ran away
She asked someone else to give him water
questions.correctAnswer: She gave him water and also watered his camels
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:18-20 describes how Rebekah gave the servant water and then drew water for all his camels.

questions.question: What did the servant give Rebekah after the camels had finished drinking?
options: A golden earring and two bracelets of gold
A silver necklace
A robe and a crown
A bundle of spices
questions.correctAnswer: A golden earring and two bracelets of gold
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:22 states the servant took a golden earring and two bracelets for her hands after the camels finished drinking.

questions.question: Who was Rebekah's brother who came out to the well to meet the servant?
options: Laban
Nahor
Bethuel
Abraham
questions.correctAnswer: Laban
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:29 says Rebekah had a brother named Laban who ran out to the man at the well.

questions.question: True or False: The servant refused to eat until he told Laban and Bethuel his errand.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:33-34 says the servant would not eat until he had told his errand.

questions.question: What did Abraham's servant say had blessed his master greatly?
options: Flocks, herds, silver, gold, servants, camels, and asses
Only flocks and herds
Only silver and gold
Only servants and camels
questions.correctAnswer: Flocks, herds, silver, gold, servants, camels, and asses
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:35 lists all these blessings the LORD had given Abraham.

questions.question: Which instruction comes first in Genesis 24: Abraham's servant must not take a wife from the Canaanites or Abraham tells the servant to swear an oath?
options: Abraham tells the servant to swear an oath
Abraham's servant must not take a wife from the Canaanites
Both instructions are given simultaneously
Neither instruction is given
questions.correctAnswer: Abraham tells the servant to swear an oath
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:2 records Abraham telling the servant to put his hand under his thigh and swear before instructing him not to take a wife from the Canaanites in verse 3.

medium.title: Genesis Chapter 24 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Genesis Chapter 24 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who did Rebekah identify herself as when asked about her family?
options: Daughter of Bethuel, son of Milcah, wife of Nahor
Daughter of Abraham
Daughter of Laban
Daughter of Sarah
questions.correctAnswer: Daughter of Bethuel, son of Milcah, wife of Nahor
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:24 records Rebekah saying she is the daughter of Bethuel, the son of Milcah, who was the wife of Nahor, Abraham's brother.

questions.question: What did Rebekah say about the provisions and lodging in her father's house?
options: There is no room to lodge
We have both straw and provender enough, and room to lodge in
Only enough food but no lodging
We have enough lodging but no food
questions.correctAnswer: We have both straw and provender enough, and room to lodge in
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:25 shows Rebekah assuring that they have both straw and provender enough and sufficient room for lodging.

questions.question: How did Abraham's servant respond after hearing Rebekah’s words and learning about her family?
options: He bowed his head and worshipped the LORD
He immediately asked for Rebekah's hand
He left without eating
He sent a message to Abraham
questions.correctAnswer: He bowed his head and worshipped the LORD
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:26 records that the servant bowed his head and worshipped the LORD, showing his gratitude and reverence after the favorable response.

questions.question: According to Genesis 24:27, why did the servant bless the LORD God of Abraham?
options: Because the LORD had given him wealth
Because the LORD had led him to the house of his master's brethren and not left his master destitute
Because he found water at the well
Because he met Rebekah
questions.correctAnswer: Because the LORD had led him to the house of his master's brethren and not left his master destitute
questions.explanation: Verse 27 explains the servant blessed the LORD for His mercy and truth and for guiding him to Abraham's kindred's house.

questions.question: What role did Laban play when the servant arrived at the well?
options: He ran out to meet the servant
He was not at home
He refused to speak to the servant
He sent Rebekah away
questions.correctAnswer: He ran out to meet the servant
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:29 shows Laban, Rebekah's brother, running out to meet Abraham’s servant at the well, showing hospitality and involvement.

questions.question: How did Laban respond when he saw the jewelry on Rebekah and heard her account of the man?
options: He invited the man to come in and prepared the house
He ignored the man
He asked the man to leave immediately
He demanded gifts from the man
questions.correctAnswer: He invited the man to come in and prepared the house
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:31 states that Laban invited the servant to come in, calling him blessed of the LORD, and prepared the house and room for the camels.

questions.question: What did Abraham’s servant do before eating the meal set before him?
options: He ate immediately
He told his errand first
He asked for more water
He left the house
questions.correctAnswer: He told his errand first
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:33 says the servant would not eat until he had told his errand, then Laban said 'Speak on,' indicating his readiness to listen.

questions.question: What promise from Abraham did the servant remind Laban about regarding the wife for Isaac?
options: That the wife must be from the daughters of Canaan
That the wife must be from Abraham’s kindred and father's house, not Canaanites
That Isaac should marry a foreign woman
That Isaac should marry a woman from Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: That the wife must be from Abraham’s kindred and father's house, not Canaanites
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:37-38 records the servant reminding Laban that Abraham made him swear not to take a wife from the Canaanites, but from his father's house and kindred.

questions.question: How does Genesis 24:40 teach about trusting God when facing uncertainty in a task?
options: It encourages relying solely on human plans
It declares God will send his angel to prosper the way and help accomplish the task
It advises giving up if unsure
It states that success depends on the woman's willingness alone
questions.correctAnswer: It declares God will send his angel to prosper the way and help accomplish the task
questions.explanation: Verse 40 assures trust in God’s guidance and provision, promising that He will send His angel to prosper the journey and mission.

questions.question: What conditional promise is made regarding the servant's oath if no suitable wife is found among Abraham's kindred?
options: The servant must return to Canaanites
The servant is cleared from the oath if no wife is given by kindred
The servant can choose any woman
The servant must wait indefinitely
questions.correctAnswer: The servant is cleared from the oath if no wife is given by kindred
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:41 explains that if the kindred do not give a wife, the servant is clear from his oath, showing God's allowance for human cooperation in His plans.

questions.question: What was the sign the servant prayed for at the well to identify the right woman for Isaac?
options: A woman who offered him gold
A woman who would say, 'Drink, and I will give thy camels drink also'
A woman who would refuse to give water
A woman accompanied by many servants
questions.correctAnswer: A woman who would say, 'Drink, and I will give thy camels drink also'
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:14 and verses 43-44 detail the servant's prayer that the woman who offers him water and offers to water his camels is the one appointed by the LORD.

questions.question: What does Genesis 24:46 show about Rebekah's character in responding to the servant's request?
options: She hesitated and delayed
She quickly gave water to him and also to his camels
She refused to help
She asked for payment first
questions.correctAnswer: She quickly gave water to him and also to his camels
questions.explanation: Verse 46 portrays Rebekah’s promptness and generosity, showing kindness and hospitality, traits valued in Christian living.

questions.question: True or False: The servant immediately ate the meal set before him upon arriving at Laban's house.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:33 states the servant would not eat until he had told his errand, showing his integrity and purposefulness before enjoying hospitality.

questions.question: True or False: Laban and Bethuel said the matter of Rebekah's marriage was from the LORD and that they could neither speak bad nor good against it.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:50 records Laban and Bethuel affirming the LORD's hand in the matter and their inability to oppose it, showing submission to God’s will.

questions.question: True or False: Rebekah refused to go with the servant when asked if she would leave her family.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: In Genesis 24:58, Rebekah agrees to go with the servant, showing her faith and obedience to God's leading.

hard.title: Genesis Chapter 24 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Genesis Chapter 24.

questions.question: Who did Abraham's servant identify Rebekah as the daughter of?
options: Bethuel, son of Milcah
Nahor, son of Rebekah
Bethuel, son of Nahor
Isaac, son of Abraham
questions.correctAnswer: Bethuel, son of Nahor
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:47 states that Rebekah was 'The daughter of Bethuel, Nahor's son, whom Milcah bare unto him.'

questions.question: What did Abraham's servant do after confirming Rebekah's identity and family?
options: Bowed down his head and worshipped the LORD
Offered a sacrifice
Returned to Abraham immediately
Sent Rebekah back to her family
questions.correctAnswer: Bowed down his head and worshipped the LORD
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:48 says the servant 'bowed down my head, and worshipped the LORD, and blessed the LORD God of my master Abraham'.

questions.question: What was Laban and Bethuel's response when asked whether they would allow Rebekah to marry Isaac?
options: They said it was the LORD's will and gave permission
They refused to answer
They demanded a bride price
They insisted Rebekah stay longer before deciding
questions.correctAnswer: They said it was the LORD's will and gave permission
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:50-51 states, 'The thing proceedeth from the LORD... Behold, Rebekah is before thee, take her, and go'.

questions.question: What did Abraham's servant give to Rebekah after the marriage agreement was confirmed?
options: Jewels of silver and gold and raiment
A new camel
A scroll of blessings
A house in Canaan
questions.correctAnswer: Jewels of silver and gold and raiment
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:53 notes the servant brought 'jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and raiment, and gave them to Rebekah'.

questions.question: How long did Rebekah's family want her to stay before going to Isaac?
options: At least ten days
One month
Three days
Immediately
questions.correctAnswer: At least ten days
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:55 says her brother and mother said, 'Let the damsel abide with us a few days, at the least ten'.

questions.question: How did Abraham’s servant respond when asked to delay departure?
options: He requested to depart immediately, citing the LORD's blessing
He agreed to wait for ten days
He asked for more gifts to stay longer
He insisted on staying indefinitely
questions.correctAnswer: He requested to depart immediately, citing the LORD's blessing
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:56, he said, 'Hinder me not, seeing the LORD hath prospered my way; send me away'.

questions.question: What was Rebekah's response when asked if she would go with Abraham's servant?
options: I will go
I need more time to think
I cannot leave my family
I will go only if Isaac comes to get me
questions.correctAnswer: I will go
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:58 records Rebekah's reply, 'I will go'.

questions.question: Where did Isaac go to meditate when he saw the camels approaching with Rebekah?
options: In the field at eventide
By the well Lahairoi
Inside his tent
To the city of Nahor
questions.correctAnswer: In the field at eventide
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:63 states, 'Isaac went out to meditate in the field at the eventide'.

questions.question: What did Rebekah do when she first saw Isaac approaching?
options: Lighted off the camel and covered herself with a veil
Ran to meet him openly
Sent her servants ahead
Waited on the camel without moving
questions.correctAnswer: Lighted off the camel and covered herself with a veil
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:64-65 describes that she 'lighted off the camel' and 'took a veil, and covered herself'.

questions.question: What significant act did Isaac do after Rebekah became his wife?
options: He loved her and was comforted after his mother’s death
He immediately moved to a new land
He held a feast for Abraham
He sent her back to her family
questions.correctAnswer: He loved her and was comforted after his mother’s death
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:67 states, 'Isaac... took Rebekah, and she became his wife; and he loved her: and Isaac was comforted after his mother's death.'

questions.question: The phrase 'the gate of those which hate them' in the blessing to Rebekah (Genesis 24:60) most closely parallels which Old Testament theme?
options: The promise of victory and protection for Abraham’s descendants
The building of city gates in ancient Near East
The exile of Israel to Babylon
The establishment of the Levitical priesthood
questions.correctAnswer: The promise of victory and protection for Abraham’s descendants
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:60 blesses Rebekah that her seed will 'possess the gate of those which hate them', echoing the theme of God’s protection and triumph for Abraham's line seen in Genesis 22:17 and Psalm 24:7.

questions.question: Which literary device is evident in the servant’s prayer and the subsequent immediate arrival of Rebekah?
options: Chiastic structure illustrating divine providence
Allegory of the bride and the church
Parable of the Good Samaritan
Typology of the Passover lamb
questions.correctAnswer: Chiastic structure illustrating divine providence
questions.explanation: The servant’s prayer in Genesis 24:12-14 and the immediate answer with Rebekah’s arrival in 24:15 form a chiasm, emphasizing God’s providential guidance.

questions.question: The Hebrew word translated as 'maidens' or 'damsels' in Genesis 24:61 is derived from what root meaning?
options: Young women or female servants
Warriors or protectors
Priests or mediators
Merchants or traders
questions.correctAnswer: Young women or female servants
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'na’arot' (נְעָרוֹת) used in Genesis 24:61 refers to young women or female servants accompanying Rebekah, reflecting common ancient Near Eastern household roles.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God’s providential guidance seen in Abraham’s servant’s mission in Genesis 24?
options: Romans 8:28 - 'All things work together for good to them that love God.'
Matthew 5:3 - The Beatitudes
Revelation 21:4 - New Heaven and New Earth
James 2:14 - Faith without works is dead
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 8:28 - 'All things work together for good to them that love God.'
questions.explanation: Romans 8:28 reflects the providential theme where God orchestrates events for good, paralleling the servant’s trust in God’s guidance in Genesis 24:27.

questions.question: True or False: Abraham’s servant was allowed to bring Isaac back to his homeland if Rebekah refused to go with him.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:6 clearly states Abraham warned, 'Beware thou that thou bring not my son thither again' meaning Isaac was not to be brought back if the woman refused.

theological.title: Genesis Chapter 24 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Genesis Chapter 24 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is demonstrated by God's guidance of Abraham's servant in finding a wife for Isaac, as portrayed in Genesis 24:12-14?
options: God's sovereignty in providence
God's wrath against sin
God's judgment on the Canaanites
God's patience with Israel
questions.correctAnswer: God's sovereignty in providence
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:12-14 shows Abraham's servant praying for God's guidance and God answering by directing him to Rebekah, demonstrating God's sovereign providence in directing events according to His will.

questions.question: According to Genesis 24:3-4, what specific command did Abraham give to his servant regarding the choice of a wife for Isaac, and what theological principle does this illustrate?
options: Do not take a wife from Canaanites; illustrating the principle of covenant purity
Take any wife regardless of nationality; illustrating God's universal grace
Take a wife from Egypt; illustrating God's judgment on Canaan
Do not marry at all; illustrating asceticism
questions.correctAnswer: Do not take a wife from Canaanites; illustrating the principle of covenant purity
questions.explanation: In Genesis 24:3-4, Abraham commands his servant not to take a wife for Isaac from the Canaanites but from his own kindred, illustrating the theological principle of maintaining covenant purity and separation from surrounding idolatrous nations.

questions.question: How does Genesis 24:7 reveal God's faithfulness to His promises in the Abrahamic covenant?
options: God promised to give the land to Abraham's seed and sent His angel to guide the servant
God promised immediate wealth and power to Abraham's descendants
God promised to remove all enemies from Abraham's land
God promised to establish a political kingdom for Abraham's seed
questions.correctAnswer: God promised to give the land to Abraham's seed and sent His angel to guide the servant
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:7 recounts God's promise to Abraham to give the land to his seed and that He would send His angel to guide the servant in finding a wife for Isaac, demonstrating God's faithfulness to His covenant promises.

questions.question: What do the gifts of gold earring and bracelets given to Rebekah in Genesis 24:22 signify in the context of the narrative?
options: They signify a betrothal and covenant commitment
They are simple trade goods with no deeper meaning
They represent payment for services rendered
They symbolize Rebekah's wealth independent of the marriage
questions.correctAnswer: They signify a betrothal and covenant commitment
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:22 shows the servant giving Rebekah gold jewelry, which in the ancient Near Eastern context signifies betrothal gifts, symbolizing a covenant commitment between her and Isaac.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is illustrated by Abraham's servant placing his hand under Abraham's thigh to swear an oath in Genesis 24:2-3?
options: The seriousness and binding nature of covenants
The doctrine of baptism
The forgiveness of sins
The priesthood of believers
questions.correctAnswer: The seriousness and binding nature of covenants
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:2-3 describes the servant placing his hand under Abraham's thigh to swear an oath, reflecting the ancient practice symbolizing the serious and binding nature of covenants and promises, a theological foundation for covenant fidelity.

questions.question: How does the servant’s prayer and the subsequent answer in Genesis 24:12-21 demonstrate the attribute of God's faithfulness?
options: God answers the servant's specific prayer by providing Rebekah exactly as requested
God ignores the servant's prayer, showing human responsibility
God punishes the servant for doubt
God sends a prophet to answer instead
questions.correctAnswer: God answers the servant's specific prayer by providing Rebekah exactly as requested
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:12-21 narrates the servant's precise prayer for a sign regarding Isaac's wife, and God's faithfulness is shown as Rebekah appears meeting exactly the criteria prayed for, validating God's trustworthiness.

questions.question: What does Genesis 24:26-27 teach about the proper human response to God's guidance and blessing?
options: Worship and praise directed to God
Immediate obedience without reflection
Self-reliance and planning
Silent acceptance without joy
questions.correctAnswer: Worship and praise directed to God
questions.explanation: In Genesis 24:26-27, the servant bows and worships the LORD, blessing Him for not forsaking His mercy and truth, demonstrating that proper human response to divine guidance includes worship and praise.

questions.question: How does the interaction between Abraham's servant and Laban in Genesis 24:49-50 reflect the recognition of divine providence in human affairs?
options: Laban acknowledges that the matter is from the LORD and refrains from opposing it
Laban demands payment before agreeing to the marriage
Laban immediately rejects the servant's proposal
Laban consults local priests for approval
questions.correctAnswer: Laban acknowledges that the matter is from the LORD and refrains from opposing it
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:49-50 records Laban and Bethuel recognizing the servant's proposal as proceeding from the LORD, indicating human acknowledgment of divine providence in significant life events.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that divine intervention in human matchmaking is a myth. What does Genesis 24:40-41 teach regarding God's involvement in the servant's mission, countering this claim?
options: God promises to send His angel and prosper the way, showing active divine involvement
The servant acts solely on human wisdom and strategy
God remains silent and uninvolved
The outcome is left entirely to chance and human decision
questions.correctAnswer: God promises to send His angel and prosper the way, showing active divine involvement
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:40-41 shows Abraham assuring the servant that the LORD will send His angel to prosper his journey, affirming God’s active role in guiding human decisions and opposing the sceptic’s claim.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight about God's providence and human responsibility is revealed by Genesis 24:5-6 and Genesis 24:10-11?
options: God directs the servant's mission, but the servant must act faithfully and diligently
God forces human actions without consent
Human effort is unnecessary if God is sovereign
The servant acts independently of God's will
questions.correctAnswer: God directs the servant's mission, but the servant must act faithfully and diligently
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:5-6 shows the servant’s concern and Abraham’s command, while 24:10-11 records the servant taking camels and traveling, illustrating that while God providentially guides, human responsibility and faithful action remain essential.

questions.question: How does Genesis 24:63-67 contribute to the redemptive narrative by portraying Isaac's acceptance of Rebekah as his wife?
options: Isaac's love and comfort upon marriage symbolize God's provision of a bride for His Son, foreshadowing Christ and the Church
Isaac's marriage is a political alliance only
Isaac rejects Rebekah initially because of her background
Isaac remains unmarried, representing separation
questions.correctAnswer: Isaac's love and comfort upon marriage symbolize God's provision of a bride for His Son, foreshadowing Christ and the Church
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:63-67 depicts Isaac taking Rebekah as wife and being comforted, which foreshadows the Messianic theme of Christ receiving His bride, the Church, showing God's overarching redemptive plan.

questions.question: What does Genesis 24:36-38 teach about the doctrine of divine election and covenant succession through Isaac?
options: God chose Isaac as the heir of Abraham’s blessings, emphasizing covenant succession
God chose multiple sons equally for the covenant
God rejected Isaac entirely
God’s covenant had no chosen heir
questions.correctAnswer: God chose Isaac as the heir of Abraham’s blessings, emphasizing covenant succession
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:36-38 recounts that Sarah bore Isaac and Abraham gave him all his possessions, confirming divine election and covenant succession through Isaac as the chosen heir.

questions.question: What combined teaching about divine guidance and human consent is conveyed by Genesis 24:48 and Genesis 24:58?
options: God leads the way, but Rebekah’s willing consent is necessary for the covenant to proceed
God forces Rebekah to go without choice
Human consent is irrelevant to God’s plan
Divine guidance is only symbolic, not practical
questions.correctAnswer: God leads the way, but Rebekah’s willing consent is necessary for the covenant to proceed
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:48 shows the servant worshipping God for guidance, and 24:58 records Rebekah agreeing to go, teaching that divine guidance and human free will cooperate in covenant fulfillment.

questions.question: How does the narrative in Genesis 24:30-32 illustrate the theological theme of hospitality and covenantal relationship?
options: Laban invites the servant in, providing provisions and lodging, symbolizing covenant hospitality
Laban refuses to host the servant
Laban demands payment for lodging
Laban doubts the servant’s story and sends him away
questions.correctAnswer: Laban invites the servant in, providing provisions and lodging, symbolizing covenant hospitality
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:30-32 records Laban welcoming the servant, preparing the house and provisions, exemplifying hospitality as a sign of covenant relationship and blessing in biblical theology.

questions.question: What doctrinal lesson about prayer and divine response can be drawn from the servant’s specific request and its immediate fulfillment in Genesis 24:14-21?
options: God hears and answers faithful, specific prayer according to His will
God ignores human prayers
Prayer is only symbolic and has no effect
Divine response is always delayed
questions.correctAnswer: God hears and answers faithful, specific prayer according to His will
questions.explanation: Genesis 24:14-21 shows the servant praying for a specific sign and God immediately providing Rebekah who fulfills the sign, illustrating the doctrine that God actively hears and answers prayer.
